fullPassage: Coral reefs are being threatened by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this. They intend to record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs that are suffering from severe bleaching. A healthy reef is noisy, and it is believed that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live. Damaged reefs, on the contrary, are silent. They attract few new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further. The researchers tested their idea at a reef severely affected by bleaching. Healthy reef sounds were played in certain locations for 40 days. At the end of this period, the researchers found that the areas where the sounds were played had attracted twice as many young fish as places that were left silent.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) threatened=위협받는 / protected=보호받는 (B) noisy=시끄러운 / silent=조용한 (C) safely=안전하게 / dangerously=위험하게
det.analysis:
① threatened—noisy—safely: 따뜻한 물에 '위협받고(threatened)', 건강한 산호초는 '시끄럽고(noisy)', 어린 물고기가 '안전하게(safely)' 살 수 있는 곳 ←정답
② threatened—silent—dangerously: (B) 건강한 산호초는 시끄러움 (C) 안전하게 살 수 있는 곳
③ protected—noisy—dangerously: (A) 백화·죽음을 유발하니 '보호'가 아니라 '위협' (C) 안전하게
④ protected—silent—safely: (A)(B) 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 따뜻한 물의 위협(threatened) → 건강한 산호초는 시끄러움(noisy) → 안전하게(safely) 사는 곳

det.analysis:

det.tip: 시끄러움이 물고기를 끌어들임(attracts) → 손상된 산호초는 조용함(silent) → 더 악화됨(degrade)

det.korean: play: (A) (소리를) 틀다·재생하다(동사) (B) 놀다(동사)
det.analysis:
① (A) 틀다·재생하다 (B) 놀다: 녹음한 소리를 '틀다', 아이들이 공원에서 '놀다' ←정답
② (A) 놀다 (B) 틀다·재생하다: (A)(B) 뒤바뀜
③ (A) 연주하다 (B) 놀다: (A) 소리를 '재생'하는 것이지 악기 '연주'가 아님
④ (A) 틀다·재생하다 (B) 연기하다: (B) 공원에서 '노는' 것이지 '연기'가 아님
det.tip: play의 다의어: (소리를) 틀다·재생하다 vs 놀다

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "an animal that lives in a particular place"

det.korean: researcher=연구자 / predator=포식자 / visitor=방문객 / inhabitant=서식 동물, 주민
det.analysis:
① researcher: 연구자 — 특정 장소에 사는 동물이 아님
② predator: 포식자 — 사냥 여부의 개념, 정의와 다름
③ visitor: 방문객 — 잠깐 들르는 것이지 사는 것이 아님
④ inhabitant: 특정 장소에 사는 동물(주민) ←정답
det.tip: lives in a particular place(특정 장소에 산다) = 서식 동물(inhabitant)

questions.passage: Coral reefs are being __________ (threaten) by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: threaten(위협하다) → threatened. 'be being + 과거분사'(진행 수동태) '~되고 있는 중이다'
det.analysis: threaten을 과거분사 threatened로 바꿔요. 'are being threatened'는 'be동사 + being + 과거분사(p.p.)' 형태의 진행 수동태로 '위협받고 있는 중이다'라는 뜻이에요. 산호초가 따뜻한 물에 의해 '위협을 당하는' 쪽(수동)이라서 과거분사(threatened)를 써요.
det.tip: be being + 과거분사 = ~되고 있는 중이다. threaten → threatened

questions.passage: A healthy reef is noisy, and it is __________ (believe) that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: believe(믿다) → believed. 'It is believed that ~'(~라고 여겨진다) 가주어 수동태
det.analysis: believe를 과거분사 believed로 바꿔요. 'It is believed that ~'는 'It(가주어) + be동사 + 과거분사(p.p.) + that절'로 '~라고 (사람들에게) 여겨진다/믿어진다'는 수동태 표현이에요. 여기서 It은 뒤의 that절을 대신하는 가주어라서 believe를 수동형 believed로 써요.
det.tip: It is believed that ~ = ~라고 여겨진다. believe → believed

questions.passage: Coral reefs are being threatened by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this. They intend to record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs that are suffering from severe bleaching. A healthy reef is noisy, and it is believed that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live. Damaged reefs, __________, are silent. They attract few new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further. The researchers tested their idea at a reef severely affected by bleaching. Healthy reef sounds were played in certain locations for 40 days. At the end of this period, the researchers found that the areas where the sounds were played had attracted twice as many young fish as places that were left silent.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: for example=예를 들어 / on the contrary=그와는 반대로 / as a result=그 결과 / in addition=게다가
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞은 '건강한 산호초는 시끄러워 물고기를 끌어들인다', 빈칸 뒤는 '손상된 산호초는 조용하다'로 정반대 내용이에요.
① for example: 예를 들어 — 예시 관계가 아님
② on the contrary: 앞뒤가 대조 관계라 '그와는 반대로' ←정답
③ as a result: 그 결과 — 인과 관계가 아님
④ in addition: 게다가 — 추가 관계가 아님
det.tip: 시끄러운 건강한 산호초 ↔ 조용한 손상된 산호초 = 대조 → on the contrary

questions.passage: Coral reefs are being threatened by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this. They intend to record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs that are suffering from severe bleaching. A healthy reef is noisy, and it is believed that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live. Damaged reefs, on the contrary, are silent. They attract few new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further. The researchers tested their idea at a reef severely affected by bleaching. Healthy reef sounds were played in certain locations for 40 days. At the end of this period, the researchers found that the areas where the sounds were played had attracted __________ young fish as places that were left silent.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: half as many=절반만큼의 / far fewer=훨씬 더 적은 / twice as many=두 배만큼 많은 / no more=더 이상 없는
det.analysis:
빈칸 뒤 'as places that were left silent(조용하게 둔 곳들에 비해)'가 비교 단서예요. 소리를 튼 곳이 더 많은 물고기를 끌어들였다는 실험 결과죠.
① half as many: 절반만큼 — 소리가 물고기를 늘렸으니 반대
② far fewer: 훨씬 적은 — 결과와 반대
③ twice as many: 소리를 튼 곳이 '두 배만큼 많은' 물고기를 끌어들임 ←정답
④ no more: 더 이상 없는 — 결과와 반대
det.tip: 소리를 튼 곳이 더 많은 물고기 → 두 배만큼 많은(twice as many)
